title: Structural insights into selective recognition of ATP-mimicking inhibitors by the atypical kinase HASPIN
task: Determine structural basis for selective ATP-mimicking inhibitor recognition by HASPIN kinase
key_results: Crystal structures at 1.74 Å and 1.88 Å resolution; LJ-5242 binds ~10-fold tighter than LJ-5157; LJ-5242 shows ~100-fold higher selectivity in antiproliferative assays
comments: The preorganized regulatory/catalytic spines and αC helix stabilization provide mechanistic explanation for selectivity despite ATP-pocket conservation across kinomes.

hypotheses.hypothesis: ATP-mimicking inhibitors can achieve selectivity through HASPIN's distinctive ATP-binding pocket architecture
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; selective inhibition achieved with LJ-5242 despite ATP-like scaffold

hypotheses.hypothesis: HASPIN regulatory and catalytic spines are preorganized independently of nucleotide binding
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; extensive hydrophobic packing observed, particularly in N-lobe stabilizing αC helix

title: Loss of Drosophila nucleostemin 1 disrupts ribosomal protein homeostasis and rRNA processing to trigger apoptosis via the Xrp1/Irbp18 complex
task: Determine how nucleostemin 1 loss triggers apoptosis and disrupts ribosome biogenesis
key_results: Ns1 depletion reduces 65 ribosomal proteins and triggers p53-independent apoptosis via Xrp1/Irbp18-mediated JNK activation; global translation is suppressed
comments: The p53-independent mechanism in Drosophila contrasts with mammalian p53-dependent responses, suggesting species-specific regulatory differences in ribosomal stress pathways.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Ns1 is required for rRNA processing
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; Ns1 depletion impairs rRNA processing

hypotheses.hypothesis: Ns1 maintains ribosomal protein homeostasis
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; loss of Ns1 reduces 65 RPs

hypotheses.hypothesis: Apoptosis occurs via p53-dependent mechanism
hypotheses.result: Rejected; apoptosis is p53-independent and proceeds through Xrp1/Irbp18-JNK pathway

title: Hypoxia-induced upregulation of lncRNA SLC9A3-AS1 promotes lung adenocarcinoma progression through the miR-506-5p/ASPH/NOTCH1 pathway
task: Elucidate how hypoxia-induced lncRNA SLC9A3-AS1 drives lung adenocarcinoma progression
key_results: SLC9A3-AS1 is HIF-1α-activated under hypoxia; functions as ceRNA to sequester miR-506-5p, allowing ASPH overexpression and NOTCH1 activation; promotes LUAD cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and EMT
comments: The HIF-1α-lncRNA-miRNA-protein axis represents a multi-level regulatory network; therapeutic targeting of this pathway may require concurrent HIF-1α inhibition for efficacy.

model_io.model: LUAD cell lines (in vitro) and mouse tumor xenografts (in vivo)

hypotheses.hypothesis: SLC9A3-AS1 is transcriptionally activated by HIF-1α under hypoxia
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; SLC9A3-AS1 is hypoxia-responsive and HIF-1α-dependent

hypotheses.hypothesis: SLC9A3-AS1 promotes LUAD progression through ceRNA activity targeting miR-506-5p
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; SLC9A3-AS1 knockdown effects reversed by miR-506-5p inhibition or ASPH overexpression

hypotheses.hypothesis: NOTCH1 signaling is activated downstream of ASPH in this pathway
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; ASPH overexpression restores NOTCH1 activation and oncogenic phenotype

title: Synergistic enhancement of athletic performance and psychological resilience through AI-driven personalized exercise regimens network
task: AI-driven co-optimization of athletic performance and psychological resilience
key_results: Personalized group achieved +21.4% Athletic Performance Index vs. +12.0% standard; +18.6% resilience (CD-RISC) vs. +8.3%
comments: Well-designed RCT with dual-outcome optimization, but sample size (n=60) and lack of mechanistic biomarkers limit generalizability.

inputs: Physical fitness, fatigue, stress, resilience state variables

hypotheses.hypothesis: Explicit co-optimization of physical and psychological outcomes achieves synergistic adaptation beyond single-objective training
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; ablation studies showed dual-objective and adaptive feedback both critical

title: Enhanced human pose estimation via self-distilled and token-pruned transformer
task: Efficient human pose estimation via transformer compression
key_results: mAP=74.8% on MSCOCO with 13.2M parameters and 4.7 GFLOPs
comments: Practical efficiency gains, though absolute performance lags full-scale models.

title: Depression detection from multimodalities based on LeNet with hunter-geese optimization
task: Depression detection from multimodal MRI and speech data
key_results: Accuracy=91.276%, Sensitivity=92.266%, Specificity=91.000% on combined MRI+speech inputs
comments: Reasonable diagnostic performance but lacks independent external validation and clinical utility metrics.

title: A comparative study of machine learning models for microbiome-based diagnosis and multi-class staging of colorectal cancer
task: Benchmark machine learning models for microbiome-based colorectal cancer diagnosis and TNM staging
key_results: Random Forest best performer: AUC=0.8633–0.8672 (CRC vs. control), macro-AUC=0.7736–0.7816 (TNM staging); sensitivity=0.8571 for early-stage detection across 1,749 total samples
comments: Comprehensive 8-algorithm comparison across binary and multi-class tasks with robust external validation; Random Forest's dominance suggests tree-based methods well-suited to microbiome compositional data.

inputs: Fecal samples from CRC patients, controls, TNM stages

outputs: Robust performance estimates with bootstrap analysis

hypotheses.hypothesis: Microbiome composition enables accurate CRC diagnosis and TNM staging via machine learning
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; Random Forest achieves high performance on multiple independent cohorts

title: Patient-matched transcriptomics of in vivo and in vitro colonic epithelium substantiate organoids as a translational model for ulcerative colitis
task: Validate intestinal epithelial organoids as translational model for ulcerative colitis epithelial inflammation
key_results: Cytokine-stimulated IEOs replicate in vivo UC epithelial inflammation; TNF+IFNγ and cytokine cocktail concordant for >350 UC-relevant genes; protein-level validation of IRF1, ERAP2, NOS2, DUOX2 confirmed patient-dependent expression
comments: Patient-matched transcriptomics provides strong validation of IEO model relevance, though epithelial-specific mechanisms remain partially characterized.

inputs: TNF, IFNγ, IFNλ1, IL-17, IL-1β, IL-22, Poly(I:C)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Cytokine-stimulated IEOs recapitulate patient-specific UC epithelial inflammation
hypotheses.result: Confirmed for interferon signaling, antigen presentation, and UPR pathways with concordance >350 genes

title: Enhancing anomaly-based zero-day attack detection framework using CNN-driven feature extraction and OC-SVM
task: Zero-day attack detection via CNN feature extraction and anomaly detection
key_results: Accuracy=98.41% (NSL-KDD), 99.31% (CIC-IDS2017); F1-score>98% across datasets
comments: High performance on benchmark datasets, but generalization to novel attack types remains uncertain.

title: An interpretable radiomics–machine learning model for early risk stratification of invasive fungal infections in community-acquired pneumonia: a dual-center study
task: Develop interpretable radiomics-ML model for invasive fungal infection risk in community-acquired pneumonia
key_results: Combined radiomics+clinical model AUC=0.808 (internal), 0.786 (external); age and high-order texture features most influential; favorable decision curve utility
comments: Dual-center validation and SHAP interpretability are strengths; moderate incremental value suggests radiomics as adjunctive rather than definitive tool.

model_io.model: VB-net pneumonia segmentation + radiomics feature extraction

hypotheses.hypothesis: Radiomics improves early IFI risk stratification when combined with clinical data
hypotheses.result: Confirmed with AUC improvement from 0.719 (clinical alone) to 0.808 (combined)

title: POTEF upregulation drives hepatocellular carcinoma progression via oncogenic signaling and immune modulation
task: Characterize POTEF role in hepatocellular carcinoma progression
key_results: POTEF upregulation associated with unfavorable prognosis, advanced stage, vascular invasion; promotes proliferation/migration, suppresses apoptosis; positively correlates with CD163+ macrophage infiltration
comments: Solid functional validation but EMT and immune mechanisms require deeper mechanistic interrogation.

model_io.model: Xenograft and in vitro functional assays

hypotheses.hypothesis: POTEF drives HCC progression via EMT regulation and macrophage infiltration
hypotheses.result: Confirmed at expression and immune infiltration level; direct causal mechanism not fully established

title: Multi-layer feature aggregation network with residual module and attention mechanism for jaw cyst image segmentation
task: Jaw cyst image segmentation using deep learning
key_results: F1=0.9411, IoU=0.9444 on original jaw cyst dataset; F1=0.8678, IoU=0.8388 on ISIC-2018
comments: Strong performance metrics but limited to medical imaging segmentation without clear biological insights.

title: Investigation of the molecular network underlying PET-MPs-induced inflammatory bowel disease via integrated machine learning and molecular docking approaches
task: Identify molecular mechanisms linking PET microplastics to inflammatory bowel disease
key_results: Identified 14 hub genes via machine learning (GBM ROC-AUC=0.862 for CD, RF ROC-AUC=0.806 for UC); molecular docking predicted high-affinity binding to hub targets
comments: Integration of multiple ML approaches with docking is comprehensive, though causation remains speculative without functional validation.

model_io.model: Multi-machine learning ensemble (GBM, RF, SVM, etc.)

hypotheses.hypothesis: PET microplastics interact with 14 machine learning-prioritized hub genes to promote IBD pathogenesis
hypotheses.result: Favorable binding affinities predicted; mechanism remains hypothesis-generating

title: Designing a secure anonymous group-oriented key agreement protocol for the internet of medical things
task: Secure group-oriented key agreement for Internet of Medical Things
key_results: Identified 7 of 8 security objectives compromised in Chen-Lee protocol (replay, traceability, impersonation attacks); proposed modifications add ~4% overhead
comments: Practical security analysis with real-world Raspberry Pi testbed validation, though applicability to modern cryptographic standards unclear.

title: Uncovering core regulators of multi-abiotic stress adaptation in Arabidopsis thaliana through integrative meta-analysis and machine learning with RT-qPCR validation
task: Identify core transcriptional regulators of multi-abiotic stress adaptation in Arabidopsis
key_results: Identified 8 high-confidence predictive biomarkers via ensemble ML; 4 candidates (At5g50360, At1g73480, At3g46230, At1g16850) validated by RT-qPCR; correlation with 10 upregulated TFs (r=0.67–0.90) and 1 repressor (r=−0.47 to −0.74)
comments: Comprehensive meta-analysis and multi-layer validation (ML, RT-qPCR, network analysis), but functional knockouts still needed to confirm regulatory roles.

inputs: Arabidopsis RNA-seq under drought, salt, ABA stress

hypotheses.hypothesis: Hub genes (At5g50360, At1g73480, At3g46230, At1g16850) are core regulators of abiotic stress via ABA-dependent and -independent pathways
hypotheses.result: Confirmed osmotic stress induction; weak ABA responses for At3g46230 and At1g16850 suggest alternative cis-regulation

title: Saltation-consistent event-aware digital twins for uncertainty transport in non-smooth dynamical systems
task: Develop event-aware digital twin framework for non-smooth dynamical systems with uncertainty transport
key_results: Saltation-consistent transport laws for sensitivities and covariance at event surfaces; reduced-order error bounds isolate jump mismatch; benchmarks show improved post-event accuracy and parameter identification
comments: This work elegantly unifies mechanics, inference, and uncertainty propagation for hybrid systems, though computational cost and scalability to high-dimensional problems remain unclear.

model_io.model: Event-aware hybrid mechanical system with Bayesian inference
inputs: high-fidelity hybrid model (unilateral contact, friction, impulses)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Event surfaces as first-class transport interfaces improve uncertainty propagation and reduced-order fidelity in non-smooth systems
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: impact, stick–slip, and shock-response benchmarks show preserved post-event accuracy and improved transient fidelity

title: Parasitically coupled 16-port massive MIMO antenna for mmWave applications
task: Design 16-port compact massive MIMO antenna for mmWave 5G/6G
key_results: Antenna resonates at 40 GHz (37.5–49 GHz band) with 40 dB peak return loss; achieves 17.9 dB and 17.2 dB gain at 39 and 41 GHz; SAR 0.045 W/kg at 40 GHz
comments: The compact form factor (26.2×79×0.508 mm³) and coverage of multiple 3GPP bands are significant, though mutual coupling between 16 ports is not detailed.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Parasitic element coupling in compact geometry enables efficient 16-port massive MIMO operation in mmWave band
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: achieved high gain and low return loss across 3GPP bands with acceptable SAR levels

title: Metamaterial-enhanced MIMO antenna array system for non-invasive cerebral hemorrhage assessment in elderly and disabled patients
task: Design MIMO antenna for microwave imaging of cerebral hemorrhage detection
key_results: Compact T-shaped two-port MIMO antenna operating 3.1–6 GHz with ECC <0.005, diversity gain >9.9 dB, mutual coupling <−15 dB in human head model
comments: The system demonstrates strong technical merit for portable stroke diagnosis, though clinical validation of hemorrhage detection sensitivity and specificity is not presented.

model_io.model: T-shaped two-port MIMO antenna with UWB configuration

hypotheses.hypothesis: Compact MIMO antenna with low mutual coupling enables non-invasive hemorrhage detection via microwave imaging
hypotheses.result: Supported: demonstrated minimal mutual coupling and favorable isolation; hemorrhage detection capability inferred from scattering parameter sensitivity

title: Design of a slotted bowtie dual-polarized antenna for Sub-6 GHz multi-service wireless applications
task: Design dual-band dual-polarized antenna for sub-6 GHz wireless
key_results: Operating at 2.52 GHz and 4.42 GHz with port isolation >30 dB; antenna gain improved from 2 dBi to 7.14 dBi with reflector integration
comments: The reflector-assisted design effectively improves gain, though the reported impedance bandwidths (220 MHz and 420 MHz) are moderate relative to the center frequencies.

model_io.model: Slotted bowtie dual-polarized antenna with reflector

hypotheses.hypothesis: Reflector placement at optimized distance enhances dual-band operation and radiation performance
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: gain increased significantly and isolation levels exceeded 30 dB across bands

title: Riccati-based analytical framework for solving the potential Korteweg-de Vries equation
task: Solve potential KdV equation using Riccati-based analytical methods
key_results: Derived multiple families of exact traveling wave solutions including solitary, periodic, rational, hyperbolic and trigonometric structures
comments: The Riccati-based Modified Extended Simple Equation Method provides a systematic approach, though the paper focuses on analytical results without numerical validation or physical applications.

model_io.model: Potential KdV equation with Riccati framework

hypotheses.hypothesis: Extended Riccati framework can systematically generate exact solutions for nonlinear evolution equations
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: multiple solution families derived and validated by direct substitution

title: Accurate alpha-particle stopping power measurements in graphenic carbon foils and their application to high-precision, non-destructive areal density determination
task: Measure alpha-particle stopping power in graphenic carbon foils for non-destructive areal density determination
key_results: Relative energy-loss uncertainties <1%; mean excitation energies (73±2) eV (KETEK) and (85±3) eV (Applied Nanotech); areal densities ~0.2 mg/cm² determined with stopping-power model
comments: The method is precise for thin foils but limited by angular straggling and non-linear energy dependence beyond thin-target approximation; systematic differences between foils require independent validation.

model_io.model: Alpha-particle energy loss spectroscopy in graphenic carbon

hypotheses.hypothesis: Modified Bethe formalism with empirically adjusted mean excitation energy provides consistent stopping-power description across energy range
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: systematic differences in stopping power between foils align with compositional and microstructural differences

title: Community-aware biased random walks for community detection in attribute networks
task: Community detection in attributed networks using biased random walks
key_results: Adaptive community-aware random walk parameters based on node degrees and attributes; validated on real-world and synthetic datasets
comments: The method addresses practical limitations of prior random-walk approaches, though specific quantitative performance metrics (e.g., accuracy, precision) are not stated in the abstract.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Adaptive random walk parameters avoiding oversampling of low-degree nodes improve community detection
hypotheses.result: Validated on real-world and synthetic datasets; specific comparative metrics not stated in abstract
